$comment: Art manifest for Enjeu. Every icon slot in the game, and where its art comes from.
The art is sourced from The Noun Project. Noun Project icons are offered either
under CC BY (free, attribution REQUIRED) or under a paid royalty-free licence
(no attribution). Terms differ per icon and per download, so 'creator' and
'licence' below must be filled in from each icon's own page at download time.
tools/credits.py reads this file and writes CREDITS.md. It REFUSES to write
anything while a used slot is missing its creator or licence, which is the
point: an incomplete attribution page is the actual legal exposure here.
'source': null means no art has been chosen for that slot yet.
$verified: 2026-08-27: every one of the 42 sourced URLs was loaded individually. All 42
return 200, all 42 are by the same creator, Maxicons (user id 3983118),
uploaded 2019-02-13 into the collection above. 'creator' below is therefore
filled in from the pages themselves rather than guessed.
'licence' is still null everywhere ON PURPOSE, and tools/credits.py still
refuses to write CREDITS.md because of it. That is correct: each page shows
TWO licences at once (its embedded record says license=CREATIVECOMMONS, i.e.
CC BY with attribution required, while the visible buy box offers a paid
royalty-free option with no attribution). Which one attaches is decided by
which button is pressed at download time, per icon, so only the person
Two page descriptions were wrong and were corrected against the artwork:
'classes hunter' is an owl with arrows, not an archer, and 'element stream'
is a droplet, not a stream. Both still suit their slots.
Watch: the earth element sigil (element-mountain) and the Mountain biome
(landscape-mountain) are both mountains and may not be tellable apart on a
printed face. Not yet seen side by side at card size.
$boss_sizes: The five boss-size slots are left unsourced deliberately, not from neglect.
The in-house glyphs are one figure escalating: S is a bare minion, M gains
shoulders, L gains horns and outflung arms, XL gains wings, UM gains a
spiked crown. That series encodes RELATIVE SIZE, which is the information
those cards carry. Five unrelated stock creatures cannot: nobody ranks a
skeleton below a bear below a dragon by size. The collection has no
size-graded monster family to buy either (it is a skills-and-equipment set,
not a bestiary), and each card already prints its size letter at 110 units,
about 11mm on a 63mm card. Sourcing these would add five CREDITS.md rows for

$tinting: An <image> ignores the stroke colour, so downloaded art does NOT inherit the
card's colour language the way a glyph does. js/cards/face.js now floods the
wanted colour through the art's own alpha for any non-default ink. That
matters most for 'crown', which prints gold on a #111 face: untinted, an
attributed crown would print black on black and the boss life card would
come out blank. Invisible in review, obvious on paper.
